clues.title: Road lines: all white or all yellow
text: Chilean road lines are either **all white**, or **all yellow**:
- All white road lines are most common. Within the Americas, they are a good clue for Chile, though not completely unique.
- All yellow road lines are seen in National Parks or areas of high snowfall. Within the Americas, these all yellow road lines are essentially unique to Chile.
You will almost **never** see a combination of the two colours, apart from a few rare exceptions.
NOTE: It is important to note that Argentina has a decent amount of roads with all white road lines.
clues.summary: Lines are either all white (most common) or all yellow (national parks and snowy areas), almost never mixed. All-yellow is essentially unique in the Americas. Argentina also has many all-white roads.

differs.how: Argentina also has many all-white roads, but no all-yellow ones

clues.title: Google car: plain white, no antenna (older camera)
text: Chile has a solid **white** Google Car with no antenna in **Generation 3**. There are two variants:
- [A plain white car](https://maps.app.goo.gl/1nNGSJYhdk9Th3c9A) (left).
- [A white car with a visible black section](https://goo.gl/maps/sk6weUxKpaC7pAvz7) (right). This car is unique to Chile.
A blue Google Car can be seen in Generation 4.
NOTE: In Generation 3, a plain white Google Car with no antenna can also be seen in Peru and Bolivia.
clues.summary: In the older Gen 3 coverage (blurrier, softer colours): a white car with no antenna, either plain or with a visible black section (that one is unique here). Newer Gen 4 uses a blue car. Peru and Bolivia have plain white cars too.

clues.title: Pole: square concrete, indented sides, pinholes
text: Chile uses square concrete poles with an **indent** on both sides. They are somewhat similar to Brazilian poles, however have fewer horizontal supports in the indent. The upper part typically has small pinholes.
Wooden poles are also fairly common.

images.caption: A square concrete pole with indented sides, right

clues.summary: Square concrete poles with an indent on both sides and small pinholes near the top. Brazilian poles are similar but have more horizontal supports in the indent. Wooden poles are common too.

differs.how: Brazilian poles have more bars across the indent

clues.title: Plate: white private, orange commercial
text: Regular vehicles have **white** licence plates, while commercial and taxi vehicles have **orange** plates.
NOTE: Orange plates can also be seen in Ecuador. Brazilian commercial plates are red, but can look similar in some lighting.

images.caption: Chilean plates: white standard (top) and orange commercial or taxi (bottom)

clues.summary: Normal cars have white plates, taxis and commercial vehicles have orange ones. Ecuador also has orange plates. Brazilian commercial plates are red but can look orange in some light.

clues.title: Sign: slots at the top of signposts
text: **Slots** can often be seen at the top of signposts.

images.caption: Red box marks the slot at the top of the post under a blue motorway sign
Red box marks the slot at the top of the post under a blue motorway sign

clues.summary: Signposts often show slots at the top.

clues.title: Chevron: yellow with black arrows
text: Chile uses chevrons with a **yellow base **and **black arrows**.
NOTE: Argentina uses white with red arrows.
clues.summary: Chevrons are yellow with black arrows. Argentina uses white with red arrows.

differs.how: Argentina's are white with red arrows

clues.title: Bollard: Spanish style, white front, orange back
text: Chilean bollards are similar to **Spanish style** bollards, with a white reflector at the front and a yellow-orange reflector at the back. They are not super common.
clues.summary: A bollard with a white reflector on the front and a yellow-orange one on the back, like in Spain. Not very common.

clues.title: Bollard: orange temporary with two white stripes
text: While regular bollards are somewhat rare in Chile, you may sometimes find this **orange**, temporary bollard, with **two white stripes** at the top.
clues.summary: Normal bollards are rare, but you may see a temporary orange one with two white stripes at the top.

clues.title: Bridge: red painted fence posts
text: Bridges in Chile often have **red painted** fence posts.
clues.summary: Bridges often have red painted fence posts.

clues.title: Climate: desert north, cold wet far south
text: Shown here is a **Köppen climate map** of Chile.
Chile is a long and narrow country that spans more than 4,000 kilometres from north to south, meaning that its climate varies significantly due to latitude.

The northern parts of the country, which lie in the tropical zone, are dry and arid, leading to a mild desert climate. In the centre, around the capital, the climate becomes less arid, leading to a temperate mediterranean climate. In the southernmost regions of Chile, which lie in the subantarctic zone, the climate is cold and wet, leading to a cool oceanic climate.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: A very long, narrow country: dry desert in the north, a mild Mediterranean climate in the middle around the capital, and cold wet weather in the far south.

clues.title: Road numbers: first letter runs A to Y, north to south
text: Chile uses a memorable regional road naming system, where the first letter increases between [A](https://goo.gl/maps/5sCeUaH9QXJVz6vt9) and [Y](https://goo.gl/maps/gD4ACFHPsD4bqpC37) from **north to south**. For more information on specific regions, see [here](https://sites.google.com/site/roadnumberingsystems/home/countries/chile?pli=1).
clues.summary: Road names start with a letter that moves through the alphabet from A in the north to Y in the south.

clues.title: Phone numbers: two-digit area code then seven digits
text: Chilean phone codes will sometimes have a **two digit** area code in front, followed by seven digits. The patterns of the codes are easily memorable. Most of the central states also have different area codes for specific provinces, which can help you make accurate guesses.
clues.summary: Numbers sometimes have a two-digit area code followed by seven digits. Central areas also have separate codes per province, which helps with guessing.

clues.title: Landscape: extremely dry desert, no plants
text: The Atacama is an extremely arid desert covering the northern third of Chile. Some parts of it experience the lowest rainfall on the planet. As a result, many locations in this desert are almost completely devoid of any vegetation: you will often just see sand and bare rock without any plants in sight anywhere.
NOTE: The Atacama Desert also covers parts of southern Peru, western Bolivia and northwestern Argentina.
clues.summary: In the northern third: sand and bare rock with no plants in sight, one of the driest places on earth. The same desert also covers parts of south Peru, west Bolivia and north-west Argentina.

clues.title: Landscape: smooth sandy eroded mountains, valleys
text: The region of Arica y Parinacota can be recognized by the **smooth, sandy** mountains that may look **slightly eroded**, or have [bulbous formations](https://goo.gl/maps/SRJ52GEYhEnuRU9G6). Valleys are also common, which are rarely seen in other parts of Chile.
clues.summary: In the far north: smooth, sandy mountains that look slightly eroded or have bulbous shapes. Valleys are common, which is rare elsewhere in the country.

clues.title: Landscape: rocky uneven mountains
text: These **rocky, uneven** mountains are most commonly seen in Atacama and northern Coquimbo.
clues.summary: In the north: rocky, uneven mountains, most common in the northern desert and the region just south of it.

clues.title: Landscape: brownish-red soil
text: This **brownish red soil** can sometimes be seen in Atacama region.
NOTE: This is most reliable in Generation 3. This soil can be seen in other regions in Generation 4.
clues.summary: In the northern desert: brownish red soil. Most reliable in older Gen 3 coverage; in Gen 4 it appears in other regions too.

clues.title: Plants: eucalyptus plantations in a dry climate
text: **Eucalyptus plantations** combined with a somewhat dry climate are a good indicator that you are in southwestern Valparaíso.
clues.summary: Eucalyptus plantations with a fairly dry climate point to the south-west of the central coastal region.

clues.title: Landscape: dry hills, scattered plants
text: The region around Santiago can be recognized by its semi-arid climate, having **dry hills** and scattered vegetation.
clues.summary: Around the capital: a semi-arid climate with dry hills and scattered vegetation.

clues.title: Landscape: greener than the capital area, vineyards
text: Compared to the area around Santiago, the Maule region has a similar look. However, it has a **Mediterranean** climate, and is generally greener. **Vineyards** are also commonly seen in this region.
clues.summary: Looks like the capital area but with a Mediterranean climate, generally greener, and many vineyards.

clues.title: Plants: pines with puffy needles
text: Concepcion pines, scientifically named Pinus radiata, can be recognized by their **puffy** needles. They are most commonly found in **Bio Bio**, where the city of Concepcion is located, and less commonly in Ñuble and Araucania.
clues.summary: Pine trees (Pinus radiata) with puffy needles. Most common in the south-central coast region, less so a bit north and south of it.

clues.title: Landscape: narrow roads with trees on both sides
text: **Narrow roads** with trees on both sides can commonly be seen in the regions of Bio Bio and Araucania.
clues.summary: Narrow roads with trees on both sides are common in the south-central regions.

clues.title: Plants: monkey puzzle trees
text: **Monkey puzzles**, scientifically named Araucaria araucana, are found in far eastern Araucania.
NOTE: Monkey puzzles can also be found on the other side of the Argentinian border.
clues.summary: Monkey puzzle trees (Araucaria) grow in the far east of the south-central region. They also grow across the border in Argentina.

clues.title: Landscape: rolling farmland like New Zealand
text: A **rolling, agricultural** landscape, comparable to New Zealand, can be seen on Isla Grande de Chiloé.
NOTE: Similar looking landscapes exist in some other parts of the country, but usually more level.
clues.summary: On a big southern island: rolling farmland that looks like New Zealand. Similar views exist elsewhere in the country but are usually flatter.

differs.how: Looks like New Zealand but this is flatter in other areas

clues.title: Plants: giant cabbage-like leaves (Chilean rhubarb)
text: **Chilean rhubarb** can commonly be found on Isla Grande, and on the mainland east of it. Chilean rhubarb can be recognized by its large, cabbage-like appearance.
clues.summary: Chilean rhubarb has big cabbage-like leaves. Common on the big southern island and the mainland east of it.

clues.title: Landscape: lush green valleys, rocky peaks, overcast
text: **Lush green valleys**, with rocky mountains and often overcast coverage, can be seen in southern Los Lagos and northern Aysén.
clues.summary: In the south: lush green valleys, rocky mountains and often overcast photos.

clues.title: Coverage: autumn colours in the far south
text: Southern Aysén can be recognised by **autumn coverage**, having orange and red coloured vegetation. Keep in mind that not all coverage in this region will have fall colours.
clues.summary: In the far south: orange and red autumn leaves, though not all coverage there has them.

clues.title: Road lines: dotted paint
text: Roadlines with **dotted paint** are common in Los Ríos and Aysén.
clues.summary: In the south: road lines made of dotted paint are common.

clues.title: Road: high altitude, steep drop to a valley
text: The A-31 can be recognised by its **high altitude**, with a **steep drop** into a valley to the north. The road also has Gen 3 sunset coverage.
clues.summary: On one northern road: very high altitude with a steep drop into a valley to the north. It also has older Gen 3 sunset coverage.

clues.title: Coverage: sunset, white dome, pink volcano tops
text: Generation 4 sunset coverage can be seen on Ruta 21 from Calama to San Francisco de Chiu Chiu. In the west near Calama, the sun has just started to set, causing a giant white dome in the sky. In the east, the sky has a warm **gradient**, and the tops of the volcanoes are seen glowing pink.
clues.summary: Newer Gen 4 sunset coverage on one northern road. Near the west the sun is just setting, making a big white dome in the sky; in the east the sky has a warm gradient and the volcano tops glow pink.

clues.title: Coverage: sunset on two northern roads
text: More Generation 4 Sunset coverage can be seen on B-710 and Ruta 5.
On the B-710, a **slight ridge** can be seen to the west, while Ruta 5 is more open. Make sure to use the road angle or other clues before guessing.
clues.summary: More Gen 4 sunset coverage on two roads. One has a slight ridge to the west, the other is more open. Use the road angle or other clues.

clues.title: Road: coast road, mountain wall east, Pacific west
text: Ruta 1 is a coastal road that is easily recognized by the **wall of mountains** to the east, and the **Pacific Ocean** to the west. This image shows the various weather conditions faced on the road to help you make closer guesses.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: A coastal road with a wall of mountains to the east and the Pacific Ocean to the west. The picture shows the different weather you may see.

clues.title: Road: valley, snowy peaks, triple yellow lines
text: Part of Ruta 41 is located in a valley, with **snowy** mountains seen in the distance. Many trees and vineyards can commonly be seen toward the west. Triple yellow lines can also be seen from [this point](https://goo.gl/maps/C4gxEFDpZX1Uz6er5).

images.caption: A paved road winding through a rocky valley with snow-capped peaks

clues.summary: A valley road with snowy mountains in the distance, many trees and vineyards to the west, and triple yellow lines at some points.

clues.title: Plants: purple lupine flowers along the road
text: These **purple flowers**, named Large-leaved Lupines, can commonly be found along Ruta 240.
clues.summary: Large purple lupine flowers are common along one southern road.

clues.title: Road: all yellow lines on concrete, treeless
text: **All yellow lines** on a **concrete road** are a good indicator that you are on a paved road in the Magallanes region, in the very south of Chile. The landscape tends to be barren, grassy, and treeless.
NOTE: Ruta 9 only appears in Generation 3, whereas the other roads only appear in Generation 4 coverage.
clues.summary: All-yellow lines on a concrete road point to the far south, with barren, grassy, treeless land. One of these roads only appears in older Gen 3 coverage; the others are Gen 4.

clues.title: Landscape: snowy line of peaks and two lone volcanoes
text: A distinct landscape consisting of a line of snow-capped mountains with two other isolated, symmetrical **snow-capped volcanoes** are seen in Lauca National Park. Most of the roads are newly paved and have a smooth, dark look.

images.caption: Left: snow-capped volcano; right: circle zooms in on dark ground beside a dirt track

clues.summary: In a northern national park: a line of snow-capped mountains plus two isolated, symmetrical snow-capped volcanoes. Roads are newly paved, smooth and dark.

clues.title: Plants: tamarugo trees lining a mediocre road
text: The northern section of Pampa del Tamarugal National Reserve can be recognized by the **Tamarugo trees** lining the road. The road itself is mediocre quality, and in a consistent north-west direction.
clues.summary: In the northern desert reserve: tamarugo trees line a so-so road that heads steadily north-west.

clues.title: Landscape: vast open land, salt pans, snowy volcanoes
text: Alto Loa National Reserve can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by **salt pans** leading up to snow-capped **volcanoes**. The road running through the reserve is paved.
clues.summary: A vast open landscape, then salt pans leading to snow-capped volcanoes. The road through it is paved.

clues.title: Landscape: smooth reddish mountains, salt pans
text: **Smooth** mountains with a **reddish** tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines, with [short dashes](https://goo.gl/maps/Z18RdxWXXB2c1FAr7) in the west.

images.caption: A grey road across a pale salt flat with reddish hills

clues.summary: Smooth, reddish-tinted mountains and salt pans. The reserve uses triple yellow lines, with short dashes in the west.

clues.title: Landscape: salt pans, red sand, snowy mountain pass
text: In the west, Nevado Tres Cruces National Park can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by **salt pans** leading up to a line of mountains. The sand has a **reddish **tint.
In the east, the Google Car drives up a mountain pass with views of lightly snow-capped volcanoes and **snow **on the side of the road. The roads in the National Park are paved.

images.caption: A yellow-edged road beside a salt flat under bright sun

clues.summary: West: vast open land, salt pans and reddish sand leading to a line of mountains. East: a mountain pass with lightly snowy volcanoes and snow beside the road. Roads are paved.

clues.title: Landscape: brown roadside dirt, juniper, overcast
text: Llanos de Challe National Park can be recognized by the **brown** coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, **juniper** plants, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage.
NOTE: [Pan de Azúcar National Park](https://goo.gl/maps/QyUDrkEedZ29m21G8) looks similar, however has less vegetation.

images.caption: A dirt track through rocky desert with dark hills behind

clues.summary: Brown dirt at the roadside, patches of light sand, juniper plants, dark mountains and mostly overcast skies. A similar park nearby has less vegetation.

clues.title: Landscape: vast treeless land, triple yellow lines
text: A **vast**, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and **high altitude** feel. [Monkey puzzles](https://goo.gl/maps/j5q5VVZamhkFDLSQ6) are also seen toward the east.
NOTE: Ruta 181 leading up to the reserve also has triple yellow lines, however, is less vast with more vegetation.

images.caption: A road with double yellow lines lined with tall monkey puzzle trees
A road with double yellow centre lines through dry hills

clues.summary: A vast, mostly treeless land with triple yellow lines and a cold, high-altitude feel even if dry. Monkey puzzle trees appear to the east. The road leading up has triple yellow lines too but is less vast and greener.

clues.title: Road: dense plants, triple yellow lines, tar snakes
text: Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and **tar snakes** are frequently seen. In the east, many [**dead trees**](https://goo.gl/maps/vvvheTYM3U7XohwK9) can be seen with a lack of leaves.
clues.summary: Dense plants beside the road, triple yellow lines and many tar snakes (crack-repair lines). In the east, many leafless dead trees.

clues.title: Landscape: slight sandy ridge, gradual slope
text: A **slight, sandy** ridge with a **gradual** incline can be seen in Arica.
clues.summary: A slight, sandy ridge with a gradual slope, in the far-north coastal city.

clues.title: Landscape: large towering ridge
text: A **larger, towering** ridge can be seen in Iquique.
clues.summary: A bigger, towering ridge behind a northern coastal city.

clues.title: Landscape: rockier, more uneven ridge
text: A **rockier**, and more **uneven** ridge can be seen in Antofagasta.
clues.summary: A rockier and more uneven ridge, in a northern coastal city.

clues.title: Houses: clay brick walls with triangle tops
text: San Pedro de Atacama can be recognized by its **clay brick** walls, commonly with triangles at the top.
clues.summary: Clay brick walls, often with triangles at the top, in a northern desert village.

clues.title: Sign: orange street signs at almost every junction
text: **Orange street signs** can be seen at almost every intersection in the city of Lanco, and occasionally in the nearby town of Malalhue.
clues.summary: Orange street name signs at nearly every intersection in one small southern city, and occasionally in a nearby town.

clues.title: Houses: orange-stained wood, mountains to the east
text: Villa O’Higgins can be recognized by the large **mountains** located immediately to the east. To the west, [snow-capped mountains](https://maps.app.goo.gl/QGUzYaHWvb8PphP99) are seen in the distance. Street signs, fences and many other structures throughout the village are made of orange-stained wood.
clues.summary: A village with large mountains right to the east and snowy peaks far to the west. Street signs, fences and many buildings are orange-stained wood.

clues.title: Streetlight: orange lamps
text: Orange lamps can most often be seen in Calama and Chañaral, and rarely in Antofagasta.
NOTE: Orange lamps can rarely be found in other smaller cities. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
clues.summary: Orange street lamps are most common in two northern cities and rare in a third. They rarely appear in smaller cities, so check other clues.

clues.title: Streetlight: green dome lamps
text: Lamps that look like **green domes** can be seen in Copiapo.
clues.summary: Lamps shaped like green domes, in one northern city.

clues.title: Streetlight: lamps with photocells
text: Lamps in Santiago very commonly have **photocells**. You will rarely find them in other cities such as Valparaiso, Osorno and Loncoche.

images.caption: Red circle and arrow zoom in on the lamp head with a photocell

clues.summary: The capital's lamps very often have a light sensor on top. Rarely seen in other cities.

clues.title: Streetlight: grey, thin flat top, rounded underside
text: Grey lamps with a thin, flat top and a **rounded underside** can be found in Talca.
clues.summary: Grey lamps with a thin flat top and a rounded underside, in one central city.

clues.title: Streetlight: blue rectangle with yellow stripe
text: **Blue rectangular** lamps with a **yellow stripe** can be found in Concepción.
clues.summary: Blue rectangular lamps with a yellow stripe, in one south-central city.

clues.title: Streetlight: silver top, grey bottom
text: This lamp, with a **silver top** and **grey bottom**, can be found in Puerto Montt and Temuco.
clues.summary: Lamps with a silver top and grey bottom, in two southern cities.

clues.title: Pole: white with black number vs yellow
text: Poles in Arica feature **white** paint with a black number, while the other cities in the Atacama Desert feature poles with [**yellow**](https://goo.gl/maps/xfQm8JHGpC6VCDR47) paint. Keep in mind the paint may have faded, making it look white.
clues.summary: In the far-north city the poles are white with a black number. Other desert cities have yellow poles, but faded paint can look white.

clues.title: Pole: round black poles
text: **Round** poles with black paint can be seen in the town of El Salvador.
clues.summary: Round poles painted black in one northern mining town.

clues.title: Google car: towing white-silver trailer
text: The Google car can be seen towing a **white and silver trailer** with the word ‘Outback’ south of the Chilean National Zoo in Santiago.
clues.summary: The Google car pulls a white and silver trailer with the word Outback, south of a zoo in the capital.

clues.title: Google car: grey pickup, gear, antenna front right
text: A **grey** Toyota Hilux, with various gear loaded and a **snorkel** on the front right, can be seen from around Baños Morales to [this point](https://goo.gl/maps/SWHeb1yv3ppVSbBTA), where the trekker continues the journey on foot.
clues.summary: A grey Toyota Hilux pickup with gear loaded and a raised antenna pipe on the front right. The walking backpack continues on foot from a certain point.

clues.title: Google car: white truck, mirrors, front antenna
text: Conguillio National Park can be recognized by this **white truck** with visible side mirrors and an antenna on the front right.
clues.summary: A white truck with visible side mirrors and an antenna on the front right. It marks one national park.

clues.title: Google car: white pickup with visible side mirrors
text: Puerto Williams, the southernmost town covered by street view, can be recognized by this **white** pickup truck with visible side mirrors.
NOTE: The Puerto Williams coverage is located fairly far away from the normal car coverage in Chile. The nearest normal car coverage is in Fuerte Bulnes, near Punta Arenas.
clues.summary: A white pickup with visible side mirrors in the southernmost town covered. Its coverage is far from the normal car coverage; the nearest is near a southern city.

clues.title: Coverage: many radio telescopes, barren and snowy
text: The Atacama Large Millimetre Array can be recognized by the many radio telescopes in a barren, snowy environment.
clues.summary: Many radio telescopes in a barren, snowy place.

clues.title: Coverage: big radio telescopes and rural facilities
text: ALMA OSF can be recognized by the large radio telescopes and rural facilities.
clues.summary: Large radio telescopes with plain rural buildings around them.

clues.title: Coverage: horse-mounted camera
text: This **horse trekker** can be seen to the northeast of San Felipe.
NOTE: A similar trekker can be found on the other side of the border in Argentina.
clues.summary: A camera carried on a horse, north-east of a central town. A similar one exists across the border in Argentina.

clues.title: Coverage: sharp peaks, glacier walkers, orange helmets
text: The Torres del Paine area can be recognized by the **sharp peaked** mountains, and the trekker walking on a **glacier** along with other people in orange helmets.

images.caption: Circle highlights two hikers on a glacier below jagged peaks

clues.summary: Sharp-peaked mountains and the camera walking on a glacier among other people wearing orange helmets.

clues.title: Google car: leafy stick on the back
text: In Arica and Iquique, in the very North of Chile, sometimes there'll be a little stick with a few leaves stuck on the car's back.

images.caption: A leafy stick poking up at the bottom of the frame, on the back of the Google car

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: In the far north, a small stick with a few leaves is sometimes attached to the back of the car.

clues.title: Landscape: lone snowy volcano, yareta, feather grass
text: East of Putre, Ruta 11 enters Lauca National Park which has a flatter landscape, with tall snow-capped mountains in the background, and features unique Andean Plateau vegetation like Peruvian feather grass and the recognizable cushion plant yareta (Azorella compacta). You can also find Chilean bollards lining the road, which are extremely rare.

Lauca can look very similar to other areas in the east Andes of northern Chile, but it’s recognizable for the iconic Volcán Parinacota, a tall snow-capped volcano that stands alone and away from other mountain ridges. It’s visible from basically every location in the park, though it can be shrouded by clouds.

images.caption: Labels point to Peruvian feathergrass on the left roadside and bollards on the right, on Ruta 11
A snow-capped volcano above a gravel road

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A flat high plateau with tall snowy mountains behind, Peruvian feather grass and cushion-shaped yareta plants. Chilean bollards line the road (very rare). A tall snow-capped volcano stands alone, away from other ridges, and is visible almost everywhere in the park.

clues.title: Plants: copao cactus
text: Eulychnia acida, commonly known as cactus ácido or copao, is a cactus species endemic to Chile, where it is primarily distributed in the semi-arid regions of the country. Its range includes: Atacama Region, Coquimbo Region,and Valparaíso Region.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A tall cactus (cactus ácido, or copao) found only in this country, in the semi-arid north and north-centre and the central coast.

clues.title: Landscape: green river valley with railway, fan palms
text: Along the Lluta River, the Ruta 11 passes through a wide valley lined by sloping, sandy mountains that often feature distinctly round rock protrusions. The valley is home to a large amount of agriculture relative to other parts of the Atacama Desert. You’ll often see sizable green fields lined by bushes, trees, or wooden fences, as well as bunches of planted Mexican fan palms. A railroad track also follows the Lluta River on both sides, so if you’re in a green valley next to both a river and a railroad, you’re almost certainly on Ruta 11.

images.caption: Green fields with pale sand dunes rising behind
A hazy sandy mountain slope above a green valley
Green crop fields at the foot of pale desert hills
A tall maize field below pale arid hills
Two tall palm trees in front of a bare sand dune

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A wide valley with sloping sandy mountains that have round rock bumps, lots of farmland by desert standards, green fields with bushes or wooden fences, planted fan palms, and a railway following the river.

clues.title: Road: new wide road, yellow barriers, red sand hills
text: After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. This section of Ruta 11 features:
Many concrete barriers (which are often painted yellow), double guardrails, and roadside drainage ways.
Maroon-colored asphalt in some places.
Mountains are made of light reddish sand with occasional exposed rock. Rounded protrusions are also common
The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.

images.caption: A paved road along a pale rocky cutting, with the road number painted on the surface

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A newly paved, wide road climbing out of the valley: concrete barriers (often yellow), double guardrails, drains, sometimes maroon asphalt, and light reddish sand mountains with round bumps. No plants at first, then small green bushes further east.

clues.title: Plants: Chilean wine palm
text: It is endemic to a small area of central Chile between southern Coquimbo, Valparaíso, Santiago, O'Higgins, and northern Maule regions. They are highly concentrated around Viña del Mar.
